description: One backup event, and — the part that makes it a control — whether anybody has ever restored from it. An unverified backup is a belief. The failure it exists to prevent is discovered exactly once, at the worst possible moment, and the sentence is always the same: the job had been green for months and the restore did not work. So this record holds the job AND the test restore, and the recovery objectives the pair is measured against.

fields.description: What was copied. `Offsite Replica` is kept distinct from `Full` because a full backup sitting on the same machine as the data answers a disk failure and nothing else — and the difference is exactly what a continuity question asks about.
fields.label: Backup Type
fields.options:
Full
Incremental
Database
Files
Offsite Replica

fields.description: How the job ended. `Partial` is its own value rather than a shade of Success: a backup that skipped what it could not read is a backup missing exactly the files that were in use, which is the set that matters.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: Where the copy actually is — a bucket, a NAS path, a drive somebody takes home. Specific enough that a person under pressure could go and get it.
fields.label: Location

fields.description: Whether this copy is somewhere the primary site's fire would not reach.
fields.label: Offsite

fields.description: How long this copy is kept before it is rotated out.
fields.label: Retention (Days)

fields.description: RECOVERY POINT OBJECTIVE, in hours: how much work the operation has decided it can afford to lose. It is a decision, not a measurement — and writing it down is what lets a backup cadence be judged against something other than a feeling.
fields.label: RPO (Hours)

fields.description: RECOVERY TIME OBJECTIVE, in hours: how long the operation has decided it can be down. The test restore below is what says whether the objective is real.
fields.label: RTO (Hours)
Test Restore — What Makes This A Control

fields.description: NOT TESTED IS THE DEFAULT AND IS NOT A FAILURE — it is the honest state of most backups most of the time. It is also what the verification control counts: a window with no Pass in it is the finding, regardless of how many jobs ran green.
fields.label: Test Restore Result

fields.description: How long the restore actually took, in minutes. This is the number that answers the RTO — an objective of four hours and a restore that took nine is a finding nobody would otherwise have.
fields.label: Restore Duration (Minutes)

fields.description: What was restored, where to, and what was checked afterwards. A restore nobody verified the contents of is a file copy.
fields.label: Test Restore Notes
Ingest Key
fields.description: Set by the backup status ingest (box|set|kind) so re-reading a status file never writes a second row.

fields.label: Test Ingest Keys
fields.description: Every test restore the ingest has already applied to this row, one per line.
